entries.title: Track — Slow + clean, six tracks at a time (120 BPM, 2:00)
entries.note: The Fruity Loops note turned into an actual constraint. The previous take asked for instruments to change and got all of them changing at once, because "the lead hands off" says nothing about what the other twelve tracks are doing — so this brief carries a voice budget of six and every section names what is silent as well as what plays. Section C runs on four tracks and no drums at all. 120 BPM buys the guitar its slowness twice over: the tempo drops and the phrasing is still held to about a note per bar. Chip blips are cut to a single accent in section F, banned from carrying the melody. At 120 BPM a bar is two seconds, so 60 bars is two minutes exactly.
entries.referenceIntent: battle_rotate_chip_150_2m with the MIDI game effects almost removed, far fewer simultaneous parts, a much slower guitar and tempo, and a pristine clean mix
entries.prompt: Composition plan, not a single prompt — the exact plan is in battle_clean_slow_120_2m.meta.json. Stated on every section: at most six instruments sound at the same time, every other track is silent until a later section; arranged like a sequencer project with fifteen tracks where only a few are enabled at once, changing per section; instruments enter and leave between sections rather than all playing throughout; pristine clean studio mix with no static, no hiss, no vinyl crackle, no bitcrush, no noise floor and clear separation between parts; the synth guitar is extremely slow, roughly one held note per bar or slower, huge sustain and long tape delay tails; 8-bit chip blips are almost absent, at most one brief accent in the whole track and never the melody; the low end keeps its submarine character as clean recorded metal creaks pitched into the sub bass with no noise around them; parts pan across the stereo field and fade in and out between sections. Banned: more than six instruments playing at once, busy cluttered mix with everything sounding at the same time, chiptune lead carrying the melody, constant arcade blips, static or hiss or vinyl crackle or bitcrush or audible noise floor, fast guitar or sixteenth-note runs or shred solo, the same lead instrument playing for the whole track, fading out to silence at the end, ending or final chord, vocals of any kind, trailer braams, EDM anthem or festival build or big drop, anthemic chorus or triumphant climax, supersaw stabs, sidechain pumping, constant sixteenth-note tick, one note repeated nonstop on a fixed subdivision, metronomic percussion, unchanging drum pattern, repetitive two-note keyboard ostinato, four-on-the-floor kick, percussion louder than the melody, chill lounge mood. Sections, eight bars each unless noted, each listing what plays and what is silent: A arpeggio, pad, creaking sub bass, hats, one sustained tone and faint machine ambience — guitar, keyboard, electric piano, chip, kick and snare and snaps all silent; hats fade in, arpeggio carries the melody. B slow synth guitar lead, pad, creaking sub bass, kick and snare, hats, machine ambience — keyboard, electric piano, chip, arpeggio, snaps, electronic percussion silent; guitar holds one note per bar. C low part on four tracks — creaking sub bass, machine ambience, one sustained tone, metallic snaps; everything else silent including all drums. D buildup — arpeggio, analog bass, kick and snare, filter sweep, electric piano, snaps; guitar, keyboard, pad and chip silent. E slow guitar solo — guitar, pad, analog bass, kick and snare, hats; everything else out of its way; single notes held across whole bars. F keyboard solo — keyboard, electric piano, creaking sub bass, kick and snare, electronic percussion; the single chip accent lands early here and does not return. G the drums take over the rhythm the keyboard was playing as the keyboard drops out — kick and snare, electronic percussion, creaking sub bass only, all melodic instruments silent. H (4 bars) turnaround on arpeggio, pad, creaking sub bass and hats, straight back to the opening, no ending.

entries.title: Track — Rotating leads + chip + creak bass (150 BPM, 2:01)
entries.review: Too many things going on at once — some parts need to stop. The MIDI game effects should be reduced to almost none. The guitar has to be way slower, and probably the whole track at a lower BPM. Wanted: arranged like a Fruity Loops project where fifteen tracks exist but only about six play at a time, changing by section. Everything very clean, no static. Replaced by battle_clean_slow_120_2m.
entries.note: A new track rather than another pass at the last one. The organising idea is that nothing plays the whole way through: the lead hands off between chiptune, synth keyboard, synth guitar and finally the kit, and the beat and melody are allowed to leave and come back. Section G is an explicit instrument handoff — the drums take over the rhythm the keyboard was playing — and H is the drum solo with only the creaking sub bass under it. This is the first brief allowed to use fades, which the loop-body bans had forbidden outright; the narrower ban on fading out to silence at the end replaces them so the track stays usable. 76 bars is 2:01.6, the reachable length nearest two minutes with every section a whole number of bars.
entries.referenceIntent: New track: fading and panning beat/melody, old-school MIDI game effects, keyboard solos, submarine creaking bass and snapping, slow heavy synth guitar solo, drum solo after the buildup, instruments changing throughout
entries.prompt: Composition plan, not a single prompt — the exact plan is in battle_rotate_chip_150_2m.meta.json. Stated on every section: the beat and the melody fade in and out across sections instead of running constantly; parts sweep across the stereo field, panning left to right, with ping-pong delay on the leads; old-school MIDI game colour — 8-bit arcade blips, chiptune square-wave leads, FM stabs and retro sweeps as accents and countermelody; the low end has submarine character, creaking metal groans pitched into the sub bass, hull stress under the music; sharp metallic snaps and cracks as percussive accents; solo leads phrase in half time against the 150 BPM bed, long held notes across bars; only one lead solos at a time and they hand off rather than stacking; the lead instrument changes from section to section rather than one carrying the whole track. Banned: the same lead instrument playing for the whole track, every part playing continuously without dropping out, static stereo image with everything centred, guitars playing fast sixteenth-note runs, shred metal solo, acoustic drums only with no synthetic percussion, fading out to silence at the end of the track, ending or final chord, vocals of any kind, trailer braams, EDM anthem or festival build or big drop, anthemic chorus or triumphant climax, supersaw stabs, sidechain pumping, constant sixteenth-note tick, one note repeated nonstop on a fixed subdivision, metronomic percussion, unchanging drum pattern, repetitive two-note keyboard ostinato, four-on-the-floor kick, percussion louder than the melody, chill lounge mood. Sections, eight bars each unless noted: A chiptune square-wave lead carries the melody while the kit fades in across the section, creaking sub bass underneath. B synth keyboard solo on a bright FM lead with portamento, chip blips answering from the opposite side of the stereo field. C low part — melody and beat fade out almost entirely, creaking submarine sub bass and metallic snaps carry the section alone. D buildup — chiptune arpeggio climbs, filter opens, kit fades back in with tom fills, panning sweeps widen. E slow heavy synth guitar solo, sustained notes held for bars with tape delay and plate reverb, thick and deliberate, other parts step back. F high part — synth guitar and synth keyboard trade phrases, full arrangement, retro FM stabs punctuating. G the keyboard figure is handed to the drums, which take the same rhythm the keys were playing, keyboard dropping out as they pick it up. H drum solo — kit alone with only the creaking sub bass, toms and snare and electronic hits, no fixed pattern. I chiptune lead and synth guitar fade back in over the drum groove, bass returns with the creak character intact. J (4 bars) short turnaround straight back to the opening chip melody, no ending.

entries.title: Ambience — Knocks + creaks (1:30)
entries.note: The approved 30s ambience at three times the length with the metal events brought forward — knocks, taps, creaks and stress groans now sit clearly above the drone bed while the drones themselves stay pulled back. Conditioned on song Ad6NttFKrgYmqAplDaZO at medium strength. Nine ten-second sections rather than three: at ninety seconds the risk is not that one density is wrong but that any density outstays its welcome, so every section states its own and none repeats its neighbour — scattered, clustered, nearly empty, close hull shift, stereo-spread knocks, quiet, busiest, winding down, sparse. Knocks forming a rhythm between themselves is banned, which is the failure mode of making discrete events louder.

Banned: creaks or knocks arriving on a regular interval, knocks forming a rhythm between themselves, loud drones or whirrs dominating the mix, harsh startling bangs or gunshot-like cracks, drums or percussion of any kind, steady beat or pulse or groove, chord progression, clear melody or hook, song structure, guitar, sonar ping beeping on a regular interval, quiet sparse intro, fade in, fade out, ending or final chord, vocals of any kind, trailer braams, EDM anthem, anthemic climax, supersaw stabs, sidechain pumping. Sections, ten seconds each: 1 establish the derelict machine interior with understated engine room drones, a few solid knocks and one long creak unevenly spaced, faint detuned sustained tones, tonal centre F sharp minor. 2 a cluster of two or three knocks close together then a long gap, a stress groan answering from further away. 3 nearly empty, one distant knock and a long quiet stretch, a faint tone bending slowly. 4 close creaking as the hull shifts nearby with a long loud groan, smaller metal pops following as the plates settle. 5 knocks move around the stereo field, one left one right, far apart in time, a motor winds up deep in the hull. 6 quiet stretch of drones and hiss almost alone, one creak arriving late and closer than expected. 7 the busiest section, knocks taps and creaks overlapping at uneven intervals with faint electrical arcing behind. 8 the motor winds down, two spaced knocks and a long structural groan. 9 sparse and unresolved, single distant creaks with long silence between them, bed at the same level it started at, no ending.

entries.title: Ambience — Subtle whirrs + random creaks (30s)
entries.review: Wonderful — this is the ambient non-music direction. Only change wanted is the knocks and metal sounds, the random creaks, a little louder. Carried forward into ambient_knocks_creaks_90s. Held back from a default generator run so it cannot be overwritten.
entries.note: The kept ambience with its own contents turned down and discrete creak events added over the top. Conditioned on song HmdxDgCWg5KkI7234mHn at medium strength — high would have carried over the levels this is meant to pull back. Three ten-second sections rather than two fifteens, so the creak events land in three different densities instead of settling into a pattern across one long stretch: scattered, then clustered, then sparse. Randomness is stated as a rule and regular creak intervals are banned, since the failure mode for a repeated event is becoming a pulse.

entries.title: Ambience — Metal creaks + submarine whirrs (30s)
entries.review: Keep. Wants the sounds already in it made a little more subtle, and actual random creaking noises added on top. Carried forward into ambient_creaks_subtle_30s, which is conditioned on this take rather than replacing it. Held back from a default generator run so it cannot be overwritten.
entries.note: Sound design rather than a track: the creaks and whirrs that have been sitting behind the music, on their own. Two standing rules had to be lifted for it — the rhythm direction and beat bans describe a fault a pulseless piece cannot have, and the ban on hiss and noise would have fought the brief, since a hull under pressure is largely made of it. Length is stated in milliseconds rather than bars because there is no pulse to align to. Pitched loosely around F# minor so it can sit under the battle tracks if that turns out to be useful.

entries.title: Sample — Three guitars + creaks (150 BPM, 1:30)
entries.note: The 7/10 take with three things added and nothing removed. Three named guitar flavours instead of one — synth/MIDI guitar on top, overdriven electric in the middle, clean chorused electric sustaining below — all phrasing in half time against the 150 BPM bed, with the fast motion left to the arpeggio and the kit. Creaking is promoted from one item in the ambience to the subject of it. Naming the flavours separately is what stops layered guitars collapsing into one thicker guitar, and unison playing is banned for the same reason.

entries.title: Full — Keys + machines (150 BPM, 4:03)

Banned: reggae skank, organ church tones, vocals, choir, trailer braams, orchestral stabs, vocal chops, shred guitar solos, djent chugs, catchy pop hooks.

entries.prompt: Instrumental only, no vocals, no choir, no spoken word. Only a few things playing: soft MIDI synth melody far back, gentle analog pad, occasional random sci-fi accents (short metallic ticks, filtered noise blips, tiny telemetry chirps, granular dust). No drums yet, no guitar yet, quiet and patient. PHASE 2 (middle ~15–20 seconds): slowly add layers — soft keyboard / electric piano melody, mutating analog arp, light percussion entering, tension rising, still not full. PHASE 3 (final ~20–25 seconds): GRAND main section / chorus payoff. Hero electric synth-guitar solo — expressive, sustained, ascending, tape delay and plate reverb, not shred-metal, not blues rock. Keyboard / synth solo lines weaving behind and under the guitar. Drums come through clearly now: punchy live-feel kit driving the grand section. Bass and pads swell wide. Keep scattered random FX in the background throughout all phases, but never louder than the melodies. Contrast is the point: soft sparse MIDI atmosphere into a grand guitar-and-keys climax. Banned: starting already full, flat energy the whole time, vocals, choir, trailer braams, orchestral stabs, djent, pop vocal chops, naming any commercial artist or game soundtrack.
